subject: Post-call recap: payment ops owners, approval lanes & next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@pondsideanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap: payment ops owners, approval lanes & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today, Sophie — great conversation. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps on the procurement/payment side.

Summary from our call:
- Pondside is evaluating Redwood for real-time inference across two products (analytics dashboard + embedded recommendations).
- Preferred commercial path today: Marketplace listing preferred for speed, but finance may push PO/contract for spend visibility.
- Key questions: who is the economic owner for budget approval, who signs contracts, and will procurement require a PO or is a card ok for initial pilots?

Immediate asks / next steps (what I can do):
1) If you can confirm the economic buyer (name/title) and the finance sponsor who will approve spend, I’ll map the signatory path and propose a tailored MAP (mutual action plan).
2) I’ll attach a short checklist comparing PO vs card flows and a draft MAP for your procurement team to review.
3) If marketplace is a hard requirement, let me know which marketplace (AWS/GCP/Marketplace partner) and I’ll prioritize the marketplace onboarding checklist.

Rough timing: we can circulate a 1-page MAP today and target a procurement touchpoint next week (Dec 22–23) if that works for you.

Attachments: RI-PO-vs-Card-checklist.pdf (short decision matrix), Pondside-MAP-v2.xlsx (draft milestones).

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0148

From: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@pondsideanalytics.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Abrams <tom.abrams@pondsideanalytics.com>, procurement@pondsideanalytics.com
Date: 2026-12-18T17:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: payment ops owners, approval lanes & next steps

Thanks Rafael — this is perfect. Quick answers:
- Economic buyer: Tom Abrams (Head of Data Products). He owns the budgets for analytics products.
- Finance sponsor: Ilya Petrov (Finance Business Partner) usually signs off on pilot spend; Ilya is copied on procurement emails but we can introduce him if needed.
- Signatory path: For pilots < $25k, product/corp can sign; for > $25k legal needs to review and our GC signs.
- Marketplace: We prefer marketplace purchases for Q1 pilots (AWS Marketplace first), but procurement will still want a PO/commit if we exceed pilot thresholds.

I’ll introduce Ilya and Tom to you in a follow-up if that helps. We’re good to get the MAP and checklist — goal is to start a pilot in January.

Best,
Sophie
Senior PM, Product Partnerships
Pondside Analytics

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T18:12:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Pondside - procurement readiness & approval mapping (post-call)

Internal note — copying you all so we can align on ask/owners before I introduce the finance/legal stakeholders.

What Pondside confirmed (from Sophie):
- Economic buyer: Tom Abrams (Head of Data Products) — budget holder.
- Finance sponsor: Ilya Petrov (Finance BP) — approves pilot spend.
- Pilot threshold: <$25k product/corp sign; >$25k requires legal review and GC signature.
- Marketplace preference: AWS Marketplace preferred, but procurement wants PO if commit > pilot threshold.

Our objectives:
1) Prepare a 1-page MAP that shows two parallel paths: (A) Marketplace fast track (pilot via AWS Marketplace, card or marketplace billing) and (B) Contract/PO path (contract, PO, GC sign) for committed spend.
2) Map the internal Pondside approver lane: Economic buyer (Tom) -> Finance sponsor (Ilya) -> Legal (GC) -> Signatory.
3) Identify Redwood owners for each milestone: Rafael owner for MAP coordination, Marissa for pricing/discount approvals, Karthik for commercial terms & legal touch, Camila to own marketplace onboarding tasks.

Requesting: Marissa, can you confirm a recommended discount and standard pilot terms for a 3-month pilot at ~20k ARR equivalent? Karthik — can you note any known legal redlines that typically block GC for pilots (e.g., data residency, IP, indemnity caps) so I can flag them upfront? Camila — can you list required marketplace artifacts and typical time to onboard (AWS listing cadence)?

I’ll hold off on intros to Ilya/Tom until we have the MAP and the two-path plan to present.

Thanks — Rafael

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-19T09:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Pondside - procurement readiness & approval mapping (post-call)

Heads up on legal points — quick bullets we should include in the MAP before intros: 
- Data residency: clarify where inference logs/metrics live; GC will ask about retention and deletion windows.
- Liability/indemnity: pilots usually ok with standard limits but GC may push for exceptions if there is sensitive PHI.
- SLA/credits: we should propose a limited SLA for pilot with optional uplift on production.
- PO vs card: if procurement insists on PO and contract, allow a 2–3 week buffer for legal review; marketplace = fastest but sometimes procurement still requests an internal PO for accounting.

Also add: if they want an on-prem or private deployment later, cost/ops discussions will change signatory expectations.

I’ll drop suggested contract bullet language and a short redline checklist into the MAP draft by EOD.

- Karthik
Director, Commercial Contracts

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Pondside - procurement readiness & approval mapping (post-call)

Thanks team — I reviewed the attached checklist and made two edits (pricing band suggestions + pilot term language). Attaching updated files and a single-slide MAP for Rafael to send.

Pricing guidance:
- Pilot (3 months): $18k total (invoiceable either via card or PO). If they go to production within 90 days, apply a 12% conversion credit on pilot spend toward first year commit.
- If they want marketplace listing only, we recommend standard marketplace list price and reserve 5% partner margin (we can top-up with a rebate for pilots).

Attachments I uploaded to the Drive link: RI-PO-vs-Card-checklist.pdf (updated), Pondside-MAP-v2.xlsx (with pricing & redline checklist). I also created a short one-slide MAP: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1MAP-slide-Pondside

Rafael — once you get an intro to Tom and Ilya, send the one-slide MAP + the checklist and suggest a 30-minute procurement-specific sync next week. I can join to handle commercial questions.

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
